exercise.name: Smith Machine Incline Press
library_steps: Set an incline bench so the bar comes down to your upper chest.
Grip slightly wider than your shoulders and twist the bar off the hooks.
Lower the bar to your upper chest, then press it back up.
exercise.one_line_summary: Lying on a 30 deg incline bench under a Smith bar that runs on fixed rails. Picture 1: bar just above the upper chest, forearms vertical; picture 2: bar pressed straight up on the rails, arms nearly straight.

setup.target: 30 deg incline, bench placed so the bar meets the upper chest.
Pronated, a little wider than the shoulders; bar path fixed by the rails.

muscles.emg: Upper pec 122-124 % MVIC at 30-45 deg (S3); Smith and free bench give similar pec activity (S1).
muscles.role: Library primary 'chest'; incline so upper chest primary.
muscles.surface: Upper front of the chest below the collarbone.

muscles.emg: Sternal head works less at incline (S3).
Anterior deltoid similar Smith vs free (S1).

muscles.role: Less needed on a Smith machine: the rails balance the bar (S1).

mistakes.mistake: Bench too far forward or back
mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Bar lands on the neck or the belly.
mistakes.why_it_matters: The rails fix the path, so the bench sets where it lands (S1).

sources.citation: Schick EE, Coburn JW, Brown LE, et al. A comparison of muscle activation between a Smith machine and free weight bench press. J Strength Cond Res. 2010;24(3):779-784.
sources.what_it_gave: Smith machine vs free bench: pectoralis and anterior deltoid similar; medial deltoid higher with free weight (the rails steady the bar).

sources.citation: Rodriguez-Ridao D, Antequera-Vique JA, Martin-Fuentes I, Muyor JM. Effect of five bench inclinations on the electromyographic activity of the pectoralis major, anterior deltoid, and triceps brachii during the bench press exercise. Int J Environ Res Public Health. 2020;17(19):7339.
sources.what_it_gave: Bench inclinations 0-60 deg: 30 deg gives the highest clavicular pectoralis activity; anterior deltoid rises with incline.

sources.citation: Lauver JD, Cayot TE, Scheuermann BW. Influence of bench angle on upper extremity muscular activation during bench press exercise. Eur J Sport Sci. 2016;16(3):309-316.
sources.what_it_gave: Upper pectoralis 122-124 % MVIC at 30 and 45 deg incline (mid concentric); lower pectoralis ~100 % at -15 deg decline, 72 % at 45 deg.

clip_check.target: 45 deg -> 106 deg (bar straight above its start) (start 35-55, end 95-115)

clip_check.check: Machine parts meet the hands/feet; levers keep their length
clip_check.target: moving rod lengths equal at start and end (+-1 cm)
